output_text: {"regions":[{"label":"Figure 9.6 — Steps to integrating the private sector into the national data system","kind":"diagram","bbox":[0.093,0.591,0.796,0.942],"summary":"Three overlapping, progressively layered panels outline steps for establishing fundamentals, initiating data flows, and optimizing the national data system for private-sector participation.","details":"The diagram uses three overlapping rounded panels. Left/orange panel, “Establishing fundamentals”: (1) Infrastructure policies — construct national transmission networks for high-speed wireless broadband access; (2) Human capital — equip workers and businesses with the skills and appliances needed to produce and use data. Center/green panel, “Initiating data flows”: (1) Infrastructure policies — increase IXPs and data centers to improve the efficiency of data transfers; (2) Incentives — adopt compensation and noncompensation schemes to promote data exchanges; (3) Data demand — promote the role of data stewards in business. Right/blue panel, “Optimizing the system”: (1) Incentives — increase data interoperability through adoption of stringent data quality and privacy standards that are also pro-business; (2) Infrastructure policies — promote expansion of and access to colocation data centers; (3) Trust — engage business through trusted data intermediaries. Source: WDR 2021 team. Note: Categories overlap and are meant to be illustrative. IXPs = internet exchange points. The panels overlap visually; they present categories/steps, not an explicit directional flow or quantitative scale.","limitations":"No quantitative values, axes, or explicit arrows are shown."}]}
